'''The eleventh house''' is the oldest rumor in [[the Banner-lands]] — the possibility, insisted upon by no reputable source and extinguished by none, that the Ten Great Houses were once eleven.

No chronicle asserts it. The rumor lives in miscounts:
* The people call the founding war the '''War of the Eleven Banners''' — eleven banners on the field, where the record counts ten.
* The [[Chronicle of Victory]]'s own swearing-account describes ''eleven lords'' coming together on the cooling ground — and ''ten'' Great Houses pressing their seals, "as they have always been ten." The discrepancy stands in plain sight, unexplained.
* The [[Ash Oath]] bears ten seals — ''some say eleven'' — and one unidentified hand wrote in a margin: ''Count the seals.''
* A children's rhyme counts ''"…eight, nine, ten, and one who left."'' Children count to eleven without knowing it.
* The people's name for [[The seat of power|the seat of power]] — '''Elvestad''' — hides the same number in its sound.
* The [[Ash Fragments]] describe an eleventh party that ''tried to stop the slaughter'' and was punished for it. The Fragments are burned, incomplete, and of uncertain authenticity — dangerous because they are credible.

What would it mean, if it were true? The sources do not say. Whether the gap in the record is the work of coordinated human power — burned chronicles, forbidden names, scraped-away seals — or of something that made the realm ''forget'', no source can tell, and the ones who asked too loudly are counted among [[The Marginal Notes|the vanished]].

''Where the sources disagree, the disagreement is kept.''
